llm_output.note: A disciplined screening cascade reduced 201 evaluated baskets to zero executed trades, with no anomalies detected and the system operating within normal risk parameters.
llm_output.reason: No deterministic anomalies were flagged, reconciliation was clean, and the zero-order outcome reflects expected-value and capital-preservation gates functioning as designed rather than a system malfunction—warranting a normal posture with continued monitoring.
llm_output.wsj_summary:
On the final trading day of July 2026, the quantitative screening framework processed 26 signal events across an evaluated basket of 201 instruments. The relative-return streak gate—a filter designed to identify securities exhibiting sustained directional momentum sufficient to warrant mean-reversion analysis—admitted 28 candidates, representing a roughly 14% passage rate from the full evaluated universe. Of those 28 streak-qualified baskets, only 9 cleared the subsequent Bayesian reversion probability threshold, underscoring the stringency of the win-probability calibration layer that sits between raw momentum identification and trade-eligibility determination.

Downstream of the Bayesian filter, the option-spread expected-value and capital-preservation decision engine produced a conservative allocation posture. Two candidates received "selected" status, four were vetoed on risk or valuation grounds, and 20 were deferred pending further confirmation. Notably, zero orders were ultimately submitted to the execution layer, indicating that even the two selected candidates failed to clear the final expected-value hurdle or that prevailing capital-preservation overrides remained active. No deterministic anomalies were flagged during the session, and reconciliation records were empty, suggesting the system operated within its designed tolerances despite the null-execution outcome.
